Welcome to the clinic. I see you have increasing pain and swelling in your right knee, along with pain during urination, and a history of a painful, swollen left ankle. To understand what is going on, I need to ask some questions.

First, have you noticed any fever, chills, or a reduced need to urinate recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive arthritis (formerly Reiter's syndrome).

I have reviewed your history of urethritis, previous oligoarthritis, and current synovitis, along with your sexual history and family background. The clinical picture strongly suggests a post-infectious inflammatory condition triggered by an STI. To confirm this, I need to see the results of your joint fluid analysis and inflammatory markers. REQUEST TEST: Synovial fluid analysis, Urinalysis, HLA-B27, and STI PCR panel.
